newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower in lack lustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower in lack lustre trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed lower on profit-taking by speculators as investors and financial institutions stayed on the sidelines, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 3.64 points lower at 698.88.
"The market was unable to maintain higher levels as profit-takers preferred to book profits at every rise," said Vikas Puri of stockbrokers Puri Financial Portfolios.
Reliance Industries saw fresh selling and dropped 2.05 rupees at 184.70 and TISCO shed 2.15 rupees at 166.95 rupees.

Shares of the State Bank of India, the country's largest public sector banking firm, fell 3.70 rupees at 219.60 while TELCO lost 11.75 rupees at 406.25, mainly due to selling by Bombay-based oeprators and mutual funds.
Shares of tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC plunged five rupees at 261 rupees following increased selling in the latter part of the session, though they had risen to 269.50 rupees in early trade.

Shares of engineering giant Larsen and Toubro dropped 2.70 rupees at 220.65 and Asian Hotels Ltd edged down one rupee at 242 rupees while BSES Ltd was 1.20 rupees down at 197.05 on selective selling by profit-takers.

ACC, the heavyweighted cement stock, lost 42 rupees or three percent at 1370 (shares with a face value of 100 rupees) on selling by mutual funds but Hindustan Lever Ltd rose 17.50 rupees at 807.50 rupees on heavy buying by foreign instituional investors (FIIs).
